title: User account
purpose: Create or maintain a staff or client account while preserving attributed laboratory history.
summary: Create or change one staff or client account: identity, client link, role groups, permissions and active state.

tasks.title: Create an account
steps: Enter [[Username]] and [[Email address]], then set a password or turn off password-based authentication.
For a client portal user, choose the [[Client]] (opening Add portal account on a client organization's page chooses it for you). For staff, leave it blank and choose [[Groups]].
Select [[Save]]. The form reopens with the remaining options.

tasks.title: Give or remove a role
steps: Move groups between Available groups and Chosen groups under [[Groups]], then select [[Save]].

tasks.title: Grant a capability
steps: Under [[User permissions]], choose the accounts permission Can view patient information, or add a group that grants it. Then save.

tasks.title: Stop someone from signing in
steps: Clear [[Active]] and save. Accounts are never deleted.

tasks.title: Sign someone out everywhere
steps: Under Sessions, select [[End sessions]], give a reason and confirm. The person can sign in again unless you also clear [[Active]].

good_to_know: Staff status and Superuser status grant no laboratory role and no capability.
Clear the client link before giving an account staff flags, groups or permissions.
You cannot deactivate the last active staff superuser or remove their Staff or Superuser status. The Scheduled jobs account cannot be changed.
If someone else saved the account after you opened it, your save is refused and nothing changes. Open the account again and redo your change.
Account and role changes are recorded in the audit history, without password values.

sections.title: Access and page variants
paragraphs: The administration site requires an active account with Staff status. User and group pages additionally require Superuser status; a laboratory admin role alone or individual model permissions do not open them. These technical flags do not themselves confer operational roles or capabilities.

Add user includes Username, Email address, Password-based authentication, Password, Password confirmation, Client, Groups, Staff status and Superuser status. New users default to Active even though Active is not on this add form. After creation the change form exposes the remaining account options. Change user groups fields into Personal info, Client access, Laboratory roles, Account status and technical access, Important dates (read only) and Sessions (read only); Compromised password (read only) follows Password.

items.label: Username
items.description: Required unique identifier, at most 150 characters; Unicode letters and digits plus @/./+/-/_ are accepted. Saving creation rejects case-insensitive duplicates; ordinary edit uses the model’s exact username uniqueness constraint.

items.label: Email address
items.description: Required syntactically valid unique account email in both add and change forms. This field is not an EmailAddress verification record or a client contact. Creation does not send an invitation or verification email.

items.label: Password-based authentication
items.description: Creation only: Enabled by default or Disabled. Enabled requires both password fields; Disabled sets an unusable password and ignores them. No alternative login provider is configured by this choice.

items.label: Password / Password confirmation
items.description: Creation: required matching password when Enabled. A new account's first password needs at least 15 characters whatever the second sign-in factor rule, and common and expected passwords and ones too similar to the username or email address are refused. No required kinds of character.

items.label: Password
items.description: Change only: read-only password-hash status, never the original secret. Reset password or Set password opens the separate administrator password form; changing this display is not password entry. The Scheduled jobs account shows its status only: nobody signs in as it, and no password can be set.

items.label: Compromised password
items.description: Change only; read only. Whether the account's password is marked as compromised now: when and by whom, while the person must choose a new one, or Not marked with the Mark as compromised link, which opens a page to mark it with a reason. Shows why instead for a shared demonstration account or an account without a password; the Scheduled jobs account shows a dash. Any new password lifts the mark.

items.label: First name / Last name
items.description: Change only; optional, each at most 150 characters, used for operator display and searching.

items.label: Client
items.description: Optional client selection. Blank means internal laboratory account; a selected client limits portal records to that client. Clear the link before granting staff flags, groups or permissions. Related-object maintenance shortcuts appear only when their registered model and permission allow them. Changing the client of an account that has portal access resets that access, recorded in its history: no linked contact, no sites, not the whole organization. The account then sees only the tickets it raised until staff set its access again on the organization's page. An account stays a laboratory account or a client portal account for life: setting a client on a laboratory account, or clearing it on a portal account, is refused; create a new account instead.

items.label: Groups
items.description: Optional assigned groups in Available groups and Chosen groups, with filter boxes, choose/remove controls and Choose all/Remove all. Built-in group names determine roles. Custom groups can carry explicit permissions without becoming operational roles. Removing a role or a capability waits for a change the person is saving at that moment, which is kept; a change they start afterwards no longer has that role or capability. A role or a group's Can view patient information grant can bring the account under the laboratory's second sign-in factor rule (Security settings), from its next sign-in.

items.label: Active
items.description: Change only; controls whether the account may authenticate and have operational access. Clear instead of deleting a historical contributor. Clearing it returns the person's tickets that are not closed to their teams' queues, unassigned, and the confirmation says how many; a ticket assigned to them while you save is either returned with the others or refused. A change the person is saving at that moment, such as a note, finishes first and your save waits for it; one they start after it is refused. A client's reply on one of their tickets that is being saved at that moment is kept, and the ticket is still returned to the queue.

items.label: Staff status
items.description: Allows the maintenance-site entry check; does not grant laboratory roles, superuser status or model permissions. Where the laboratory's second sign-in factor rule covers accounts that can open the admin console, an account with Staff status must also set up an authenticator app at its next sign-in.

items.label: Superuser status
items.description: Enables Django permission bypass for administration; does not grant laboratory roles or any capability.

items.label: User permissions
items.description: Change only. Available user permissions/Chosen user permissions assign explicit capabilities, such as the accounts permission Can view patient information. Groups can grant the same capability. Neither a role, the admin role nor Superuser status implies one, and model permissions do not replace laboratory role or ownership checks. Removing a capability waits for a change the person is saving at that moment.

items.label: Last login
items.description: Change only; read only. The date and time the person last finished signing in, recorded by the application. It is not a complete login history.

items.label: Date joined
items.description: Change only; read only. The date and time the account was created.

items.label: Open sessions
items.description: Change only; read only, under Sessions. How many sessions of the account are open and inside the session limits when the page opens, never their browsers or addresses, with the End sessions link, which opens a page to end them all with a reason. The Scheduled jobs account shows the count without the link.

sections.title: Integrity and history
paragraphs: Client isolation, last-active-superuser preservation and immutable historical actors are checked by this administration implementation. Existing built-in groups cannot be renamed in group editing. Capabilities such as viewing patient information are held only through an explicit permission. Account/role changes are audited with before/after snapshots; secret values are omitted. The change form carries the account as it was drawn. Saving waits for another change of the account being saved at that moment, then compares: if anything the page shows has changed since it was drawn, the save is refused and nothing is recorded, so a page opened earlier cannot put back an older email, name, role or status. The comparison is with the values the page was drawn with; roles count by which ones the account holds, so renaming a role on the role group page changes no account and does not refuse it. Roles and permissions are saved as the difference between those values and your choices, so a role given by other means after the comparison is kept. The audit's before values are the account as read under that wait, and its after values are what this save made.

items.label: Save
items.description: On Add user, saves and normally opens the new change form so you can edit remaining options. On Change user, saves and returns to the user list. Popup creation returns the selection to its opener. On Change user, the save is refused with the message that someone else saved this account when any value the page shows (username, names, email, client, groups, permissions, Active, Staff status or Superuser status) changed after you opened it, by another administrator, the person or the application; nothing is saved. Open the account again to see the current values. A change of the password or the sign-in time meanwhile does not refuse the save and is kept: a save writes only the fields this page edits.

items.label: Save and continue editing
items.description: Saves and opens the user change form.

items.label: Save and add another
items.description: Saves and starts a new user add form.

items.label: History
items.description: Change only: opens Django object administration history.

items.label: Delete
items.description: Never available for users; direct deletion is refused.

items.label: Home / app / Users / View site
items.description: Breadcrumbs return through administration; View site returns to the operational application. Validation errors retain non-secret form input for correction.
